acceptance: Unknown platform raises in strict and non-strict modes, with a test per platform key class.
Rewrites are expressible as translate_sql_query arguments; text processors removed or restricted; adapters migrated; golden corpus unchanged or listed.

Single registry mapping with a correctness test; bypass scanner covers the listed import forms and does not exempt sql_compat; multi-statement input handled explicitly; telemetry recorded for apply_rewrite and translate_ddl.
description: Adversarial review M6/M7/L1/L6: (M6) an unknown platform does not raise in normal runs: strict defaults to False so translate_sql_query returns untranslated source SQL (runner.py:279-297, dialect_utils.py:383-407), contradicting the ADR; unknown dialect is a configuration error and must always raise UnknownSqlDialectError. (M7) translate_sql_query still takes text pre/post-processors (interval normalizer, Q58 regex) so translation logic can live outside the fork; apply_rewrite on a string re-parses and regenerates translated SQL without identify (dialect_utils.py:437-441), re-rendering every Databricks/ClickHouse/Snowflake query; prefer passing named rewrites into translate_sql_query and applying them to the tree before generation. The platform-to-dialect mapping has three homes (adapter get_target_dialect, registry platform_family config_inheritance.py:80-91, PLATFORM_DIALECTS); the plan put it in the registry; add a test that each platform resolves to the intended dialect, not just that names resolve. (L1) the bypass scanner misses Dialect.generate, aliased transpile, optimizer imports and importlib loading, pins counts so a call can be swapped, and exempts benchbox/sql_compat/. (L6) translate_sql_query returns only the first statement silently even in strict mode; apply_rewrite/translate_ddl record no translation outcomes (schema-translation counts drop after D3).
